articles.title: Supermarket roast chicken taste test: ‘Ham-flavoured chook is extremely divisive’
articles.summary: In a bid to establish a pecking order of eight roast chooks, Nicholas Jordan samples a ‘truly neutral’ chicken and another that triggers feelings of dismay. If you value our independent journalism, we hope you’ll consider supporting us today.
body: I would guess that over the course of my childhood, 50% of all large family events featured a roast chicken. I have no idea where the chickens came from, but I know it wasn’t from our oven. Sometimes these chickens tasted as if they were baked under the care of Stephanie Alexander. Other times they had the moisture content of an Ugg boot and tasted as though they’d been seasoned by fourth-century ascetic monks. I may be exaggerating the facts here, but not my feelings.

I have since developed a deep and multifaceted interest in poultry, and was thrilled at the thought of eating eight supermarket roast chickens. Imagine your boss saying: “Don’t worry about the report, I’d rather you spend the afternoon finding deeper ways to engage in your hobby.” I wasn’t the only one – the last time there was this much interest in joining a taste test was when we tried chocolate.

Note: we also tasted Hazeldenes Free Range Sourdough BBQ Chicken (available in Harris Farm stores in Sydney) as a point of comparison. It was both the most divisive and highest-scoring chicken, mostly due to it tasting far saltier than any other chicken.

articles.title: Great to see what Tom Cruise’s belly button looks like, but it’s the stuff he is never asked about that interests me | Marina Hyde
articles.summary: Most stars, and especially women, are endlessly expected to explain the past: the lessons learned and all the regrets. But not Tom – it’s Hollywood’s free pass. There really is no press tour like a Tom Cruise press tour – which is why there have not really been any Tom Cruise press tours for a very…
body: At some level, you have to admire the mad image-industrial complex that labours to keep “the last movie star” from having to talk about the things all the other movie stars are required to lay on the line in order to promote their wares. Only a few weeks ago, Kidman was on the cover of Vogue being required to pick over her two marriages in what was otherwise the most saccharine of interviews.

Meanwhile, the world is obliged on pain of death to regard the 64-year-old Tom Cruise as ageless (and probably deathless). A few years ago, his Top Gun co-star Kelly McGillis – 62 at the time – explained why she had not been approached to return for the sequel, Top Gun Maverick. “I’m old and I’m fat, and I look age-appropriate for what my age is,” she replied with deadly affectlessness, “and that is not what that whole scene is about.”

body: Pitt, who last worked with Ayer on the second world war action thriller Fury, plays a US military special forces veteran called Belmont, tough, self-reliant and laconically good-humoured in the classic Pitt manner, now spending his retirement roaming the breathtaking remote landscape of Alaska in his seaplane. He is accompanied by his beloved service dog Odin, or Odey (played by four different German shepherds), who saw action with Belmont in various fuzzily imagined flashback combat sequences. Odin took retirement with Belmont and is now his best and only pal. Whether or not Belmont ever had a human partner is never revealed.

articles.title: Apple Is Bringing Back an Apple Watch Feature It Took Away With watchOS 27
articles.summary: Typically, software updates introduce new features rather than taking them away. So, when you install watchOS 27 on your compatible Apple Watch, you probably aren't surprised to see updates like Siri AI or a step counter on the watch face.
body: As reported by 9to5Mac, Apple quietly removed the app switcher from Apple Watches with watchOS 27. As a result, users running the beta over the summer, or those who updated in September, were likely confused when double-clicking the Digital Crown: On watchOS 26 and earlier, that gesture pulls up a menu with all open apps, similar to the app switcher on iPhone. This allows you to quickly return to a previously used app without needing to dive into the "honeycomb" main app menu.

With watchOS 27, that's no longer the case. Not only is the app switcher gone, but the honeycomb app menu has been sidelined. In their place, Apple is pushing its new "Dynamic app grid." When you press the Digital Crown once, you'll see this new menu, which features the apps Siri thinks you're most likely to use. That might include recently used apps, but also apps you frequently use, even if you haven't used them in a while.

body: After traveling across the globe and making pit stops in New York, London, Paris, and Los Angeles, Vogue World officially lands in Milan this evening.

“In the creative industry, it’s an enormous conversation at the moment,” says Vogue World Milan ’s creative director, Juan Costa Paz. “Getting into that space for this year felt like the right thing to do. Especially being in Milan, it’s such a hub for craftsmanship—Italians have always been the leaders of craft. The idea of the show really has been to create a narrative in which we can see these conversations expressed through fashion.”

articles.title: 5 Key Takeaways From ‘Swan Song,’ Charles Spencer’s New Book About Life as Princess Diana’s Brother
articles.summary: ‘Swan Song: Diana, My Sister’ has already reportedly drawn the ire of Buckingham Palace, but there’s a lot more than anti-King Charles rhetoric in the memoir.
body: There’s very little about Princess Diana ’s too-brief life that didn’t get reported on, to some degree or another, both before and after her tragic death in 1997. But now, her brother—author, journalist and broadcaster Charles Spencer, who is perhaps best-known for his searingly emotional speech at Diana’s funeral —has released a book detailing his unique perspective on life with a sister who grew up to be one of the most famous women in the world.

One of the most shocking anecdotes relayed by Spencer concerns the way his former brother-in-law spoke to him immediately following the news of Diana’s death. Spencer describes the then-Prince as sounding “giddily elated—like a lottery winner” and, on another occasion, allegedly angrily promising Charles of his late sister: “Rest assured, we’ll forget her soon enough!” That wasn’t the only time the now-King alienated Spencer by displaying callousness after a loved one’s death, though, as Spencer claims that when he was alone with Charles just after his and Diana’s father’s funeral, King Charles told him: “You’re just so lucky —you know, inheriting when you’re so young!”

articles.summary: Explore the best styling ideas from the fall 2026 runways, with standout looks from Prada, Celine, and Tory Burch.
body: The fall 2026 collections brought fresh perspective to art of styling, with plenty of recreatable ideas on how to translate the runway to real life. From Prada’s reimagining of wardrobe essentials to the inventive layering at Celine and the collision of texture and print at Marni, the season invited us to look twice and consider why and how each element works together. Styling allows you to see a knit, a pair of trousers, or a shoe in an entirely new light. It is also how we communicate our personalties and identities. Whether you lean minimalist or maximalist, utilitarian or avant-garde, the clothes you wear become an expression of who you are and how you want to be perceived.
Below, we break down some of the best looks from the fall 2026 runways—and the styling choices that made us stop and take a second look.

articles.title: ‘It’s Fundamentally Unacceptable’: A Longtime White House Correspondent on Trump’s MS NOW, CNN, and Politico Bans
articles.summary: “Just because you are not physically on the premises, it doesn’t stop us from doing our jobs,” says Ashley Parker, currently a staff writer at The Atlantic.
body: Major television networks, including ABC News, CBS News, NBC News, and Fox News, announced on Monday that they will suspend coverage of President Donald Trump in solidarity with CNN, one of the three outlets—along with MS NOW and Politico—that the president banned from the White House on Friday.

In a post to Truth Social, Trump wrote: “I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS! Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America. Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow. Thank you for your attention to this matter!”

In response, White House television pool members from ABC News, CBS News, CNN, Fox News Media, and NBC News released a joint statement on Monday, reading: “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”

articles.title: Is the New Béis Weekender Worth the Upgrade? I Took It on the Road to Find Out
articles.summary: Béis heard the complaints—here's what they did to improve, plus how it fared on the road.
body: If you’re chronically online, or just a big Béis fan, you’ve heard the chatter about its Weekender bag …and seen the videos of people schlepping through the airport with it on their shoulder, one slight breeze or accidental shoulder check from toppling over. Shay Mitchell has seen them too. After one too many comments to the effect of, “wait, does anyone really LIKE this bag?!”, the mega-popular weekender got a makeover. Relaunched in July, the redesign took some of the internet's critiques into consideration, aiming to make the bag roomier, easier to pack, and more comfortable to carry.

Side by side, the biggest difference I noticed at first glance was the size. The newer model looks larger, especially when the sides are unclipped, which adds a few extra inches of height to the bag. This seemed counterintuitive to solving the oft-repeated problem of these bags being way too heavy to carry when full, but as an overpacker, I did appreciate the added space. I was able to fit everything for my three-night, four-day trip into both bags, but with a bit more breathing room in the new one.
